title: Reduce KV hotkey thrash and simplify batcher-scheduler handshake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Symptoms: periodic tail-latency spikes in production during mixed short/long seq workloads traced to KV shard hotkey thrashing and noisy batcher->scheduler handshakes. Root cause: (1) current KV lease/eviction knobs are overly reactive to transient slot pressure and cause hot shard churn; (2) batcher emits fine-grained open/close handshake signals that force frequent scheduler reshuffles; (3) prefetch heuristics amplify oscillation. Goal: implement a defensive KV hotkey dampening layer, coarsen the batcher-scheduler handshake to explicit state transitions, and add lightweight hysteresis in slot allocation to stabilize routing and reduce tail tokens emitted per request. This is a targeted tech-debt refactor (no model changes) intended to reduce p99 token latency by ~20% on affected workloads and lower KV write amplification.
acceptance_criteria: New dampening middleware reduces KV shard hotkey eviction events by >= 50% on internal repro harness
Batcher-scheduler handshake moved to a 3-state protocol (Idle, Open, Draining) with documented state machine and tests
End-to-end integration test that injects transient load shows <10% variance in scheduler slot assignments across 30s windows
Canary rollout shows p99 token latency improvement >= 15% and no increase in error rates or request timeouts
Changes covered by unit tests, integration tests, and a new perf benchmark; PRs merged and release notes drafted
